about: What tools/blockers/check.py and live.py check against: the default filter lists of the content blockers most visitors run, read from each blocker's own catalog at check time (the lists change daily, so a release is checked against the current ones; the report records each file's address and sha256), the matcher, pinned by hash, and what AgentCake serves only for old pages.

uBlock Origin.why: uBO's lists on by default: assets.json entries of content 'filters' without 'off'; uBO filters every request, first party too

Brave.why: Brave's lists on by default (default_enabled) on the desktop; in its default Standard mode a first-party request is checked only against the lists without first_party_protections, in Aggressive mode against all of them (github.com/brave/brave-browser/wiki/Blocking-goals-and-policy)

AdGuard.why: AdGuard's own ad and tracking lists, in the uBO syntax builds; AdGuard filters first-party requests too

matcher.source: https://github.com/ArniDagur/python-adblock (Python bindings of Brave's adblock-rust); installed into a throwaway venv, never into AgentCake

legacy./rrweb-record.min.js: cake 0.3.x's recorder as a file of its own, served only for pages that still have 0.3.x's two tags (the page script has rrweb inside); EasyPrivacy blocks it by its name (/rrweb-record.min.js), which SERVER.md says

not_from_browsers./edge: the log import, sent from the web server's machine

site.why: SERVER.md's example site: the page and AgentCake's path on the same host, as its load balancer rules make them

live.why: uBO Lite, the uBlock Origin that Chrome runs (Manifest V3), with its default rulesets, in a fresh temporary profile
live.canaries_why: paths EasyPrivacy blocks by name on any site: one of them blocked shows the blocker is filtering
